candidates.statement: To be considered by the MPPRC, an issue typically should meet one or more of the following criteria:
candidates.context: Although the issue discussed by the MPPRC may have been prompted by a specific product or situation, this may lead to policy development (with due consideration of FDA’s responsibilities under its good guidance practices regulations) that may be more broadly applicable. • A novel medical policy issue requiring senior-level input. • A medical policy issue on which CDER has not taken a consistent position.

The goal of MPPRC review is to facilitate consistent communication and implementation of policies and procedures related to medical policy for internal and external use (e.g., IND drug development application review, post-approval management, labeling).

candidates.statement: Effective Date: 03/19/13, 09/16/15, 09/06/17, 02/11/21, 07/16/2026 Page 11 of 12 ATTACHMENT 2 CDER Medical Policy and Program Review Council Background Document Template Purpose - The CDER Medical Policy and Program Review Council background document is a stand-alone document of medical policy or programmatic issue(s) that require resolution from the CDER Medical Policy and Program Review Council. It should convey the medical policy or programmatic issue to be resolved, the trigger that raised the issue, and the date by which a response is needed. The document should follow the CDER Style Guide, be no more than three to five pages, and provide all the necessary information to understand the issue to be discussed.
candidates.context: 10. Life Cycle Management and impact on generic drug products Introduction - Provide an overview of the issue to be resolved. Background - Describe scientific, clinical, and regulatory areas that address the issue to be resolved. If applicable, include any areas and issues that have been raised; the regulation, MAPP, and/or guidance that has an impact on the issue; any considerations and advice already provided in discussions with the sponsor; and any other important aspect, such as previous advice and precedent given to other sponsors or staff, that would affect the resolution to be reached. The information should contain ideas, including any differing opinions, on how the medical policy should be implemented.

candidates.statement: Questions to be Considered by the Council - List the questions that the Council should consider in response to the issue to be resolved. The questions should be general, applying to all drugs and/or biological products or a group of drugs and/or biological products.
candidates.context: Introduction - Provide an overview of the issue to be resolved. Background - Describe scientific, clinical, and regulatory areas that address the issue to be resolved. If applicable, include any areas and issues that have been raised; the regulation, MAPP, and/or guidance that has an impact on the issue; any considerations and advice already provided in discussions with the sponsor; and any other important aspect, such as previous advice and precedent given to other sponsors or staff, that would affect the resolution to be reached. The information should contain ideas, including any differing opinions, on how the medical policy should be implemented. It is recommended that the questions include options with the preferred outcome highlighted, if possible.

candidates.statement: Presentation - Provide all presentation materials to be used by the individual or an identified lead from the Office seeking Council evaluation. The presentation will be limited to no more than 10 minutes and may only reference materials provided in the background document or attachments. A PowerPoint presentation is not required; however, at least one slide should be provided to display the question(s) for the MPPRC.
candidates.context: It is recommended that the questions include options with the preferred outcome highlighted, if possible. Attachments - Attach any additional background material, such as reviews, guidance, MAPPs, or regulations. Attachments are not required, but such attachments are supplementary to the Council background document.
